Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-08-14 | AAPL | Overweight | +1.1% | +2.5% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Own more AAPL, but in gated tranches, not the trader's 30% at spot. Start 10% of the planned incremental add at ~305.93 and a second 10% only if the 300.00–304.30 rising-lows floor holds on the next session. Core add requires a daily close above 309.50 on more than 60M shares (50M is only ~1.07x the 46.6M ten-day average — no confirmation) closing above both the 10EMA 309.46 and 50SMA 309.19; if the 10/50 cross has already printed, require a close above VWMA 314.11 first. Cap at benchmark weight plus 1.5–2 points until the 333.43 gap fills or an official China Apple Intelligence launch confirms. Tactical stop 292.27 on a daily close, full invalidation a weekly close below 280.50; size so even an adverse gap through 292.27 costs no more than 40–50bp of total portfolio value. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 print.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is decided by the fundamentals; only the entry is contested, which is why this is Overweight and not Buy. The bull won the fundamentals decisively: 50.06% gross margin (+357bp), revenue +16.4% to $109.42B, operating income +26.6%, operating margin 32.62%, EPS $2.02 (+28.7%), incremental operating margin 44.6%. The decisive item is the one the bear never answered — operating margin expanded 152bp through a 32.5% R&D ramp, directly refuting his core claim that R&D erodes profitability; his retreat to "forward risk" is a hypothesis, not evidence. Net cash roughly doubling to $62.2B with debt down $14.4B and no new long-term issuance, plus buybacks re-accelerating to $25.1B (+19% y/y) in the exact quarter the stock was weak, is the only management-conviction signal in the dataset. The primary trend is intact: price 9.07% above a rising 200SMA at 280.48, 50/200 spread +10.2%, no death cross in play.

The bear's tape work wins the entry, not the direction. Eleven straight closes below the 50SMA at 309.19 with failed reclaims, VWMA at 314.11 above spot so the volume-weighted buyer is underwater, an entirely unfilled 304.81–333.43 gap as overhead supply, and a decaying bounce of 75M → 68M → 49M → 46M → 34M → 28.23M (lightest since late March, ~39% below the 46.6M ten-day average). That damages the bull's "unpriced catalyst" claim: you do not get accumulation on the lightest volume in four months, and the China LLM story is a single Reuters relay with unnamed sources and a "coming months" timeline. The neutral analyst is also right that upside to 333.43 must clear 309.50, 314.11, 316.29 and 318.43 — four resistance layers, not one magnet — and that a daily-close stop does not cap a gap, as 2026-07-31 proved (333.43 to a 304.81 open on 132.5M shares).

What caps the bear's win is his own concession: he stands down on a close above 309.50 on volume, so his entire thesis lives inside a ~1.2% band, and he offers no lower terminal value — inventory math of $0.06–0.09 EPS against $54.77B of quarterly gross profit, an unquantified intangible complaint, and a real 219bp tax drag that still coexisted with 28.7% EPS growth. He states the business isn't broken. That is a timing argument, not a valuation argument, so the evidence is not balanced and Hold is wrong.

Where I overrule the trader: a 30% starter at spot is too much against MACD below zero, decaying volume, and an imminent 10/50 cross (10EMA 309.46 vs 50SMA 309.19). The conservative and neutral analysts both landed on a smaller first bite and a stricter volume filter, and they are arithmetically correct that 50M shares is not confirmation. I adopt the neutral construction — 20% split 10/10, 60M+ volume, VWMA gate if the cross prints, tilt capped at +1.5–2 points — over the aggressive full-30%-at-spot and over the conservative no-market-buy/benchmark-only stance, which assumes a better price later in a coiled range. My own record supports this: three prior AAPL Overweights (08-03, 08-05, 08-07) each bled modest five-day alpha by deploying or holding before the confirmation printed, and the 08-07 reflection named the fix — size to the arithmetic, not to conviction.

What would change it: FQ4 gross margin below 48% falsifies the margin-durability leg; a daily close below 300.00 before the 309.50 trigger means hold only the starter; a weekly close below 280.50 exits the tactical add with no averaging down; a volume close above 318.43 unlocks the final 20% toward 333.43, then 340.08/344.6. Upgrade to Buy on a volume-backed 333.43 gap fill or an official China Apple Intelligence launch plus FQ4 gross margin ≥49.5% with inventory flat-to-down. Gaps stated, not papered over: no guidance, no segment/geographic mix, no analyst revisions, no options/positioning data, no portfolio context — so sizing is a fraction of the caller's own AAPL weight; the $13.3B intangible against $13.5B of new noncurrent liabilities remains unexplained and must be verified before any add above the tilt; the late-October filing is the next real catalyst and the tape between now and then is flows, not information.

**Price Target**: 333.43

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 print

REFLECTION:
Alpha of +2.5% versus SPY over five days shows the Overweight direction was right, but five sessions is far too short to judge a 1–3 month thesis whose real catalyst is the late-October FQ4 print. The window supports the fundamentals-over-tape hierarchy — gross-margin durability and cash-return conviction were the legs that paid — and it mildly undercuts the bear's tape argument, since the decaying-volume caution did not translate into downside, though price only reached the 309.50 gate rather than clearly clearing it. The concrete lesson: with a defined invalidation at 280.50 and a 40–50bp portfolio cost cap, the 10%/10% gating left most of the position undeployed into a call I had already decided on fundamentals, so next time pre-commit more size at the floor when the risk is bounded by arithmetic rather than by tape confirmation.

[2026-08-13 | AAPL | Underweight | +2.0% | +3.9% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL at 305.26: trim 35–40% of the position to a 60–65% core, working the order over 2–3 sessions with limits rather than one print, and bias execution into the 308–310 supply zone (10-EMA 310.24, 50-SMA 309.28, VWMA 315.81) if it is offered. Base the trim at 35%; stretch to 40% only if AAPL rallies into 308–310 or if an 8.1% drawdown of the core to the rising 200-SMA at 280.30 is outside the caller's risk budget. Do not add anywhere between 300 and 309, and treat a daily close below 299.50 on >55M shares as an escalation that cuts the core further (293.50, then 280.30 are the downstream references). Re-risk in stages — first tranche on a >55M-share close above 310.30, balance on a reclaim of VWMA 315.81 — and rebuild on weakness only after a 293.50–289 test stabilizes, never on the way down. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY26 print.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is settled because all three risk seats independently endorsed reducing exposure and none defended full size — the aggressive analyst argued for a 40% trim, the conservative for a 35% base, the neutral for 30–35% with the upper bound conditioned on the core's drawdown to the 200-SMA. That is a real convergence reached from three different mandates (alpha capture, asset protection, risk budgeting), not a manufactured one, and it is why the rating is Underweight and not Hold.

The bear wins the two questions that govern this decision. First, the risk math, which the aggressive analyst framed and nobody rebutted: an entry at 305.26 with a 299.50 stop is 5.76 points, or 0.70x ATR (ATR 8.22, 2.69% of price), and the source material explicitly flags anything inside ~1.5x ATR (~12 points) in this tape as a coin flip. Raise the stop to an honest 2xATR near 289 and it sits below the lower Bollinger at 293.50, collapsing the advertised 1.8:1 to roughly 1:1. A stop that is either noise-width or edge-destroying is not a risk parameter, and the conservative analyst was right that you cannot pitch 1.9% of risk and then cite the 200-SMA at −8.1% as the backstop. Second, the tape: ten consecutive closes below a 50-SMA that is curling (309.786 → 309.277), price under the 10-EMA at 310.24 and 3.34% below the VWMA at 315.81 — meaning the average recent buyer is underwater and rallies into 308–310 are exit liquidity, not demand. MACD is −2.186 against a +0.849 signal with a −3.035 histogram, RSI sits at 43 with room to 30 (the 40.22 vs 40.34 divergence is one the report itself declines to endorse), and five-session volume of ~39.7M against a 55.1M 22-session average is a vacuum below the 50-SMA, not accumulation. The lower Bollinger has been falling (304.16 on 07-30 → 293.50 on 08-13), so it is a moving envelope, not support — which is exactly why the neutral analyst's rejection of the aggressive analyst's 293.50/280.30 pre-placed buy ladder is correct: from 280.30 a 2xATR stop lands near 264 and assumes the level holds before any evidence exists, and the 06-25/06-26 flush that rallied 19.8% is not a template because price was above the 50-SMA then and is below it now.

The bull wins the one question about the franchise, and it is why this is not Sell and why a 60–65% core is retained. Nine-month revenue +16.2% to $364.4B with gross margin 49.07% (+225 bp) and a record Q3 gross margin of 50.06% (+357 bp); EPS +22.4% and net income +20.0% even after absorbing a 219 bp tax-rate step-up worth ~2.7 points of EPS growth; FCF $110.2B (+52.4%); net cash ≈$62.2B with debt down and no new long-term issuance; a −55 day cash conversion cycle; and price still 8.90% above a rising 200-SMA at 280.30 with the 50-SMA 10.3% above it. Nothing reported has broken. The bear's forward worries — margin mean-reversion after 100% of operating-margin expansion came from gross margin, multiple compression on premium expectations, the ~$13.3B intangibles build with no matching acquisition outflow, R&D +32.5% with no attributable revenue stream, raw-materials inventory +260%, buybacks −12% and total capital return −10.1% YoY — are plausible but unquantified, and shorting a 16%-growth franchise above a rising 200-day is poor carry with demonstrated gap risk. Hence trim-and-wait, not exit.

What breaks the tie on size and mechanics. The aggressive analyst's "sell 40% to fund a reload at 293.50/280.30" overreaches by layering a second discretionary bearish trade on top of a de-risking decision; the neutral analyst's risk-budget framing and the conservative analyst's 35% base both survive that critique. The neutral analyst also supplied the correct execution note the trader's plan already implied: roughly two-thirds near 305–307, one-third into 308–310, base trim completed by the third session even absent a bounce. Against the conservative analyst, I reject leaving re-entry vague: the 08-06 GOOGL lesson is that a correct Underweight ossified into a permanent underweight when re-risk gates were stacked too far above spot, so tranche one of the add-back fires on the named invalidation level itself — a >55M-share close above 310.30 — with the balance on a VWMA 315.81 reclaim, rather than requiring MACD, VWMA and volume simultaneously.

Prior AAPL outcomes bind both ways and shape the sizing. The 2026-08-06 Underweight (−3.4% alpha, −2.2% raw) validated exactly this tape-based trim; the 2026-08-05 Overweight (−3.1% alpha) failed by deploying a starter at ~311 before its own confirmation gate; the 2026-08-04 Hold (−1.3%) demonstrated that a mid-range Hold is not free. Meanwhile the June–July Underweights (06-30, 07-01, 07-13, 07-20–07-22) each bled 3–9% of five-day alpha by trimming on momentum decay inside an intact uptrend. This setup carries what those lacked — price below the 50-SMA with a completed MACD zero-line cross and a volume-weighted cohort overhead — but it lacks the high-volume distribution print of 07-31, so the trim stays in the 35–40% band rather than going to 45%+, and the core is retained.

What would change the call: (1) flip toward Sell on a daily close below 299.50 on >55M shares (breaking the four-times-tested 300 shelf: 07-31 low 300.00, 08-03 302.56, 08-12 300.57, 08-13 302.05), on Q4 gross margin below 48%, or on 10-Q footnotes showing the +$13.2B intangibles build is a capitalized commitment carrying amortization or impairment risk; (2) flip toward Overweight on the 310.30 volume reclaim plus VWMA 315.81, gross margin holding ≥49% through the AI-competition headlines, and a signed Siri deal with disclosed terms. Explicit gaps, flagged not papered over: no Q4 revenue or gross-margin guidance/consensus, no iPhone or Pixel shipment/share data, no named Jefferies price target, no insider-transaction records (corporate buybacks are not insider conviction), no resolution of the intangibles footnote, and news coverage of only 20 of 204 records with zero items from 08-06 to 08-11 — so the picture is unknown, not clean, and the 293.50 target is technical rather than valuation-derived because no multiple or consensus series was supplied.

**Price Target**: 293.5

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 FY26 print

REFLECTION:
The five-day window shows +2.0% raw and +3.9% alpha versus SPY, so the Underweight call was directionally wrong in this sample, though five days is too short to judge a 1–3 month thesis. It undercuts the tape-based part of the thesis—ten closes below a curling 50-SMA and rallies into 308–310 as exit liquidity did not cap price—while the franchise-based case for retaining a 60–65% core was not tested. Next time, do not trim on momentum decay alone without the high-volume distribution print the thesis itself flagged as missing; require that confirmation or size the trim smaller.

[2026-08-12 | AAPL | Underweight | +4.8% | +5.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Reduce AAPL to 50–75% of a standard allocation: sell 25–50% of current exposure now into 302.25, leaning to the larger end if the position is at or above standard weight, and sell more into any rally to 309.5–311.4 (trim further toward 317.19 if volume fails to confirm the lift). Do not initiate new long capital below 311.4, and do not take the trader's tactical short at 302.25 — the stop at 311.5 is only ~1.1 ATR (8.55) inside normal noise and the payoff is ~1.4:1. Risk controls: a close below 300.00 on >55M shares cuts further, then 295.18; a close below the rising 200 SMA at 280.09 invalidates the primary trend and prompts exit of the residual. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three seats converge on reducing AAPL exposure and disagree only on whether to convert that into a short and on re-entry mechanics; the bear case wins on forward risk/reward but not by enough to justify liquidation, hence Underweight rather than Sell.

The deciding evidence is distribution, not momentum decay. The 2026-07-31 session gapped 333.43 to a 304.81 open and closed 308.91, −7.35% on 132.5M shares (~2.4x average); the subsequent bounce to 313.33 drew only 34.4M shares before rolling to a lower low at 300.57 against 302.56. Lower highs at 314.81 → 309.97 → 305.66 confirm a downtrend channel. At 302.25, AAPL is below the 10 EMA (311.35), the 50 SMA (309.48), the VWMA (317.19) and the Bollinger mid (321.22), so the July cohort is underwater and 309–317 is overhead supply. The 50 SMA has inflected down for the first time in the lookback with the 10/50 death cross ~1.87 points away, MACD is below zero with the histogram re-widening to −3.343, and RSI 40.22 is the lowest of the 40-session lookback but not oversold. This is materially different from the 2026-07-20 through 07-24 AAPL Underweights that each bled +3.2% to +3.8% of five-day alpha by selling momentum decay inside a stacked rising structure — this sells after a printed volume-distribution day and a failed bounce, the exact distinction the 2026-07-30 lesson (which earned −9.9% alpha) codified. Equally, the 2026-08-05 Overweight reflection — do not deploy even a starter before the confirmation gate triggers while the histogram widens negative — forbids buying here.

Forward-model risks all lean one way and remain unresolved: inventory +94% to $11.1B with raw materials +260%, a ~$13.3B gross-intangible step-up implying $1.3–2.6B/yr of amortization into FY2027 operating income (so 32.62% is not the forward margin base), effective tax rate up 219bp to 17.58%, R&D +32.5% versus revenue +16.4%, and buybacks cut 12% while FCF rose 52% with $48.8B parked in securities — management's own capital allocation declining to buy its stock at these prices. Gross margin at a record 50.06% against opex growth of ~22% versus revenue ~16% means the entire operating-margin expansion rests on one line item that memory/component costs can reverse, and the confirming print is not until late October.

Where the bear overreaches, and why this is Underweight not Sell: the business is not impaired — revenue $109.4B +16.4%, 50.06% gross margin, nine-month FCF $110.2B, net cash ~$62.2B, $14.4B of debt retired with zero new term debt, current ratio back above 1.0x — and price sits 7.9% above a rising 200 SMA at 280.09. The aggressive analyst's tactical short at 302.25 is the weakest proposal in the debate and the other two seats are right to reject it: the 311.5 stop is ~1.1 ATR inside single-session noise, a 2.3–3.1% rebound fills it, the payoff to 289 is only ~1.4:1, and shorting a 0.136 %B print just above the 300.00–302.56 shelf after an 11.12% nine-session drawdown bets that the next leg arrives before a normal rebound. The death cross is lagging and its stop sits exactly where the plan declares the bearish thesis wrong. Sizing guidance: express bearishness by being liquid at 285–295, not by adding gap and headline risk; any tactical short requires a failed retest of 309.5–311.4 or a close below 300 on >55M shares, at half the normal risk budget or less.

What would change it.
